name: Meyer Lemon
hook: Leaves falling off your indoor lemon tree?

steps.title: 6–8 hours of sun
steps.tip: Use your brightest south-facing window, and add a grow light if winter light is low.

steps.title: Moist, never waterlogged
steps.tip: Keep it just moist in summer. In winter, let the surface dry, then water well. Never let it sit in water.

steps.title: Bring it in before frost
steps.tip: Move it indoors gradually so the fruit doesn't drop. Keep it above 5°C in winter, away from heater vents.

steps.title: Citrus fertilizer in summer
steps.tip: Use a high-nitrogen citrus fertilizer from late March to October, then a winter citrus fertilizer, or less.

steps.title: Humid air, hand-pollinate
steps.tip: Dry air and drafts make leaves drop, so use a humidifier. Brush flowers with a soft paintbrush to set fruit.

steps.title: Check for scale and mites
steps.tip: Look for scale, aphids and spider mites. Wash the leaves before bringing it inside, and wash off any scale.

outro: Big sun, steady warmth and a paintbrush: lemons in your living room.

sources.title: Oregon State Extension: How to grow Meyer lemons successfully in the Pacific Northwest
Penn State Extension: Grow Your Own Lemons

faqs.question: Why is my lemon tree dropping its leaves?
faqs.answer: Usually cold or changing temperatures, cold drafts or dry air. Overwatering and too little fertilizer can also make leaves yellow and fall.
